career-interview-prep.content:
Question: Why do you want to change jobs?

Answer Model:
"I am looking for an environment where values align with mine and where I can focus on [My Strength] fully. My current role has taught me a lot about resilience, but I miss a team with an open and supportive culture."

(Do not badmouth former employer, focus on future.)

mitatointi.name: Invalidation & Belittling
mitatointi.desc: Continuous belittling and questioning of your skills, suggestions, and achievements. The goal is to make you feel incompetent in the eyes of others and in your own mind.
mitatointi.logExample: Manager dismissed my suggestion calling it 'useless'.

gaslighting.name: Gaslighting
gaslighting.desc: Systematic psychological manipulation where your observations, memories, and experiences are denied. You might hear phrases like 'you're imagining it' or 'you're too sensitive', until you start doubting your own sanity.
gaslighting.goal: Make the victim doubt their own sense of reality.
gaslighting.logExample: An agreed matter was later completely denied.

witness.title: Confirm the truth
actions: Say: 'I remember it that way too'

uhkailu.name: Threats & Intimidation
uhkailu.desc: Direct or veiled threats creating an atmosphere of insecurity. Hints at job loss, ruining your reputation, or vague 'consequences'.
uhkailu.goal: Silence the victim and suppress criticism through fear.
phrases: You know what follows from this
uhkailu.logExample: Manager hinted at termination without cause.

identiteetti.name: Identity Attack
identiteetti.desc: Criticism targeting personal attributes like age, gender, appearance, or background. The attack is not about your work, but about who you are.
identiteetti.goal: Humiliate as a person and create a deep sense of exclusion.
phrases: Are you too old for this?
identiteetti.logExample: My age was referred to condescendingly during training.

witness.title: Intervene in speech
witness.description: Show that this is not okay.

sexual_harassment.name: Sexual Harassment
sexual_harassment.desc: Unwanted behavior, speech, or messaging with sexual undertones. The goal is to subjugate and objectify the target based on gender.
sexual_harassment.goal: Objectify the target and create a hostile environment.
sexual_harassment.logExample: I received inappropriate comments about my appearance during break.

eristaminen.name: Isolation & Exclusion
eristaminen.desc: Active measures to prevent participation in the work community. 'Forgetting' invitations, leaving out of information circulation.
eristaminen.goal: Cut off support networks and make the victim invisible.
eristaminen.logExample: The team held a planning meeting without me.

victim.title: Break the siege
actions: Ask directly: 'Why didn't the info flow?'

ostrakismi.name: Ostracism
ostrakismi.desc: Total ignoring or 'cold shoulder'. No one answers greetings, makes eye contact, or reacts to your presence.
ostrakismi.goal: Erode human dignity and sense of belonging.
ostrakismi.logExample: No one answers my questions on the common channel.

witness.title: Break the ice
actions: Address by looking in the eyes

manager.title: Zero tolerance
manager.description: The hardest form of harassment to detect.

mobbing.name: Mobbing (Group Bullying)
mobbing.desc: A situation where one bully incites others, or the group collectively turns against one person.
mobbing.goal: Drive the victim out through massive pressure from the community.
mobbing.logExample: The whole team turned against me at the initiative of one person.

victim.title: Seek outside help
victim.description: You cannot win against a group alone.

witness.title: Be an icebreaker
witness.description: Even one dissenting voice can break the pressure.

maine.name: Reputation Damage
maine.desc: Slandering behind one's back, questioning professional credibility, and spreading false rumors.
phrases: He is not a team player
maine.logExample: False information about me was spread to management.

manager.title: Protect reputation
actions: Investigate the source of the rumor

cyberbullying.name: Cyberbullying
cyberbullying.desc: Harassment in digital channels. Nasty messages, exclusion from chat groups, or sharing humiliating material.
cyberbullying.goal: Make insecurity constant – it follows you home.
cyberbullying.logExample: Derogatory memes about me were spread in the group chat.

manager.title: Manage digital environment
manager.description: Employer is responsible for chats too.

kohtuuttomuus.name: Unreasonable Demands
kohtuuttomuus.desc: Setting workload or schedules so that success is impossible. Constant pressure and sense of rush.
kohtuuttomuus.goal: Exhaust the employee and make them feel inadequate.
kohtuuttomuus.logExample: I was given a week's work to do in one afternoon.

victim.title: Prioritize facts
actions: Make a task list with timing

epaoikeudenmukaisuus.name: Injustice
epaoikeudenmukaisuus.desc: Arbitrary and unequal application of rules, benefits, and duties. 'Yes for others, no for you'.
epaoikeudenmukaisuus.goal: Signal every moment that you are less valuable.
phrases: He gets remote work, you don't
epaoikeudenmukaisuus.logExample: Raise was denied to me without reason, given to others.

manager.title: Be transparent
manager.description: Rules are the same for everyone.

micromanagement.name: Micromanagement & Surveillance
micromanagement.desc: Stripping employee autonomy, constant watching and interfering in details without cause.
micromanagement.goal: Remove professional self-esteem and create a sense of incompetence.
micromanagement.logExample: Manager interfered with grammar and font of every email.

credit_stealing.name: Credit Stealing
credit_stealing.desc: Presenting your ideas and results as their own. Credit is taken, mistakes are left to you.
credit_stealing.goal: Advance own career at your expense.
credit_stealing.logExample: Idea I presented in meeting was recorded in manager's name.

witness.title: Restore credit
actions: Say: 'Great that you continued X's idea'

manager.title: Identify contributors
actions: Ask for breakdown of work division

unjustified_warnings.name: Unjustified Warnings
unjustified_warnings.desc: Misuse of formal disciplinary measures. Warnings for trivial matters or completely fabricated reasons.
unjustified_warnings.goal: Build a paper trail for dismissal and create fear.
phrases: You are on the black list
unjustified_warnings.logExample: I received a warning for 'attitude problem' when requesting legal break.

passiivi-aggressio.name: Passive Aggression
passiivi-aggressio.desc: Hidden hostility: sighing, eye-rolling, 'forgetting', and sarcastic praise.
passiivi-aggressio.goal: Hurt and invalidate without getting caught for direct attack.
passiivi-aggressio.logExample: Manager rolled eyes during my turn to speak.

victim.title: Make hidden visible
actions: Ask: 'What did you mean by that?'

thousand-cuts.name: Death by a Thousand Cuts
thousand-cuts.desc: Continuous series of tiny, almost unnoticeable insults and difficulties. Individually trivial, together crushing.
thousand-cuts.goal: Wear the victim out in a slow and hard-to-prove way.
thousand-cuts.logExample: Today there were 10 small unpleasant encounters.

victim.title: Quantity is quality
victim.description: Single thing is small, total is huge.

witness.title: Recognize continuum
witness.description: Do you notice a repeating pattern?

sarcasm_mockery.name: Sarcasm & Mockery
sarcasm_mockery.desc: Aggressive joking disguised as attack. If you get offended, you 'have no sense of humor'.
sarcasm_mockery.goal: Humiliate victim publicly under guise of 'humor'.
sarcasm_mockery.logExample: Two teammates mimicked my speech mockingly at lunch.

victim.title: Stay serious
victim.description: Mockery ends when it gets no audience.
actions: Ask: 'What did you mean by that?'
Don't laugh along even for politeness

neglect_indifference.name: Neglect & Indifference
neglect_indifference.desc: Complete lack of support from manager or colleagues. Requests for help are not answered, emails are ignored.
neglect_indifference.goal: Signal that you are insignificant and alone with your problems.
phrases: I don't have time now (nor ever)
strategy: Request answers in writing setting a deadline.
neglect_indifference.logExample: Manager hasn't answered my requests for instructions in two weeks.

victim.title: Demand answers
victim.description: You have right to info needed for work.

witness.title: Support info flow
witness.description: Ensure colleague isn't left in dark.

withholding_info.name: Withholding Information
withholding_info.desc: Withholding critical information needed for your work. Meetings are not informed about, instructions are not given.
withholding_info.goal: Sabotage work performance and make you look incompetent.
withholding_info.logExample: Project delayed because I wasn't informed of changed wishes.

victim.title: Protect your results
actions: Document delays due to lack of info

triangulation.name: Triangulation
triangulation.desc: Playing people against each other behind their backs. The bully tells A one thing and B another.
triangulation.goal: Break the work community and create mistrust.
strategy: Verify things directly with the person.
triangulation.logExample: Colleague claimed manager was dissatisfied, even though he was satisfied.

victim.title: Speak directly
actions: Say: 'I prefer to discuss with him'

witness.title: Don't go in between
actions: Urge parties to speak to each other

scapegoating.name: Scapegoating
scapegoating.desc: Blaming one person for collective errors or problems. 'Everything would be fine without you'.
scapegoating.goal: Shift responsibility away from management errors.
scapegoating.logExample: I was blamed for budget deficit I didn't even manage.

victim.title: Facts on table
victim.description: Guilt is manipulation, responsibility is fact.

concern_trolling.name: Concern Trolling
concern_trolling.desc: Cloaking criticism and belittling in 'friendly' concern. 'Are you sure you can cope, you look tired'.
concern_trolling.goal: Weaken victim's self-confidence without bully looking bad.
phrases: I'm just worried about your coping (mocking)
concern_trolling.logExample: Colleague sighed 'worriedly' at my desk in front of others.

victim.title: Identify toxic concern
victim.description: Real concern offers help, manipulation weakens.
actions: Ask: 'What strictly is this based on?'

victim_playing.name: Playing the Victim
victim_playing.desc: When you address the bully's behavior, they flip the situation so that you are the 'attacker' and they are the 'victim'.
victim_playing.goal: Distract attention from original misconduct (DARVO tactic).
phrases: I am bullied when I ask you to do your work
strategy: Don't apologize for things you didn't do.
victim_playing.logExample: When I remarked on shouting, colleague started crying and claimed I attacked.

witness.title: Witness origin
actions: It was about this act, not emotion

manager.title: Separate act and emotion
manager.description: Crying doesn't wipe away wrong act.

manipulaatio.name: Emotional Manipulation
manipulaatio.desc: Using emotions like guilt or pity as a control tool. 'If you cared about the team, you would do this'.
manipulaatio.goal: Get victim to act against own interests.
phrases: When you are sick, others suffer
manipulaatio.logExample: Manager guilt-tripped me about sick leave saying it destroys team spirit.

victim.title: Set healthy boundaries
victim.description: You are not responsible for other's feelings.

witness.title: Offer perspective
actions: Remind that getting sick isn't choice

manager.title: Stop the game
manager.description: Emotional intelligence must not be abused.

resources_denial.name: Resource Denial
resources_denial.desc: Denial of tools, budget, or help. You are expected to produce same results without resources.
phrases: We don't have budget for this (but others do)
resources_denial.logExample: Everyone else got new licenses except me.

victim.title: Demand tools
victim.description: Employer has obligation to provide means.

witness.title: Share yours
actions: Ask aloud why colleague doesn't have X

underemployment.name: Underemployment
underemployment.desc: Ignoring your competence and assigning too easy or useless tasks (e.g. just copying for an expert).
underemployment.goal: Humiliate professionally and force to leave.
strategy: Keep list of tasks vs contract.
underemployment.logExample: From expert tasks I was moved to do just scanning.

moving_goalposts.name: Moving Goalposts
moving_goalposts.desc: Changing goals and criteria in the middle of the process. Work is never 'good enough'.
strategy: Demand goals in writing before start.
moving_goalposts.logExample: After report finished, manager said he wanted completely different things.

victim.title: Nail down goals
actions: Remark on change's impact on schedule

spatial_harassment.name: Spatial Harassment
spatial_harassment.desc: Invading personal space (standing too close) or isolating workstation (broom closet).
spatial_harassment.goal: Make victim feel unsafe in own place.
spatial_harassment.logExample: My desk was moved to corridor even though office had space.

witness.title: Respect territory
witness.description: Taking space is use of power.

symbolic_demotion.name: Symbolic Demotion
symbolic_demotion.desc: Removal of status symbols. Downgrading title, removing name from org chart or invites.
symbolic_demotion.goal: Signal to others that victim is no longer important part of team.
phrases: He is just such an assistant
symbolic_demotion.logExample: My title was changed in email to 'intern' in front of whole dept.

victim.title: Validate your status
victim.description: Be proud of your title and work.
actions: Request grounds for changes in writing

manager.title: Respect hierarchy
manager.description: Titles and responsibilities must be respected.

hero.title: Survival Guide
hero.subtitle: When you are in the eye of the storm, we find shelter for you. Here you will find action plans, calming techniques, and the right helpers.

phase1.label: Phase 1: Acute Situation
phase1.title: Secure Yourself
phase1.description: If you have just experienced something bad, the most important thing is to restore a sense of safety. Do not make big decisions (like resigning) while in panic.

step1.content: Go to the bathroom, take a walk, or go home (report sick). You have no obligation to listen to shouting or insults.

step2.content: Log only: who, what, where, when. Do not analyze yet. Just save the facts.

step3.content: Call a partner, friend, or occupational health. Do not remain alone with the experience.

phase2.label: Phase 2: Stabilization
phase2.title: Build Defense
phase2.description: When the acute shock subsides, it is time to start collecting evidence and protecting your position.

step1.content: Use the log tool in this app. Log retrospectively all events you remember.

step2.content: Read your employment contract, occupational health guidelines, and equality plan. Knowledge is power.

step3.content: Get a document about your symptoms (insomnia, anxiety). It is important evidence that work affects health.

phase3.label: Phase 3: Resolution
phase3.title: Act or Exit
phase3.description: When you are stronger and have evidence, you can choose to fight or make a strategic exit.

step1.content: Use the ready-made templates in the reporting tool (e.g. occupational safety notification).

step2.content: If you want to leave, negotiate an exit package with the support of a union lawyer. Do not just leave empty-handed.

breathing.title: 5-5-5 Breathing
breathing.description: A physiological way to lower heart rate and stop panic reaction.

grounding.title: Grounding
grounding.description: Use senses to return yourself to this moment, away from horror scenarios.

boundaries.title: Inner Shield
boundaries.description: Practice these phrases in front of a mirror.

quotes.not_accept: "I do not accept being spoken to like that."
quotes.speak_properly: "We can continue the discussion when you speak appropriately."

darvo.title: Recognize DARVO
darvo.description: Bullies often reverse roles (Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim & Offender). Recognize the pattern.
darvo.attack_text: "You are the problem! I'm just trying to help and you start crying about everything. Are you unstable?"
darvo.response_text: They are trying to shift attention to my reaction so their actions are forgotten. I won't fall for it.

riku.title: Victim Support Finland
riku.text: If you suspect a crime (defamation, discrimination).

unions.label: Trade Unions
unions.sub: Contact your union's lawyer or shop steward.

questions.text: According to international studies, what is the prevalence of workplace bullying?
questions.explanation: International studies consistently show that 10-15% of employees experience systematic bullying.

questions.text: How many employees globally have experienced some form of violence or harassment at work during their career (ILO 2023)?
questions.explanation: ILO's first global study in 2023 showed that 23% of employed adults, or about 750 million employees globally, have experienced violence or harassment.

questions.text: Who is the most likely workplace bully?
questions.explanation: Studies show that a manager or supervisor is the most typical bully. Power hierarchy and misuse of positional power are key factors.

questions.text: What is the duration criterion for systematic bullying (Einarsen et al.)?

options.label: Once a week for at least a month
Repeatedly (e.g. weekly) and regularly for at least 6 months

questions.explanation: Einarsen defines bullying as acts that occur repeatedly and regularly (e.g. weekly) over a long period (usually at least 6 months).

questions.text: What proportion of employees have likely witnessed workplace bullying?
questions.explanation: Over 80% of employees have likely witnessed bullying at some point. This makes bystanders a much larger group than actual victims.

questions.text: What term refers to a supervisor questioning an employee's memory, perception, and sanity?
questions.explanation: Gaslighting is psychological violence where the victim is made to doubt their own reality. It silences the victim effectively.

questions.text: What is the purpose of 'constructive discharge'?
questions.explanation: The goal is to make the employee resign voluntarily, avoiding dismissal procedures. Making tasks meaningless is a common tactic.

questions.text: What does DARVO stand for?

options.label: Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim and Offender

questions.explanation: DARVO is a manipulation tactic: Deny the abuse, Attack the victim's credibility, and Reverse roles so the offender plays the victim.

questions.text: Which is a typical form of 'withholding information'?

options.label: Employee is denied access to critical info

questions.explanation: Information is power. Withholding it sets the subordinate up for failure.

questions.text: What are 'Flying Monkeys' in workplace bullying?
questions.explanation: Bullying is rarely a dyad. The bully gathers supporters who participate or silently approve.

questions.text: Which personality trio (Dark Triad) predicts bullying behavior best?
questions.explanation: The Dark Triad consists of Machiavellianism, Narcissism, and Psychopathy, predicting manipulative and unempathetic behavior.

questions.text: According to studies, which Dark Triad trait is the strongest predictor of bullying?
questions.explanation: Machiavellianism is the strongest single predictor, explaining a significant part of the variation.

questions.text: What does the Dark Tetrad add to the Triad?
questions.explanation: The Dark Tetrad adds Sadism (everyday sadism), deriving pleasure from others' suffering.

questions.text: Why is bullying often ignored in organizations?
questions.explanation: Organizations often protect 'star performers' who bring results, even if their leadership style destroys people.

questions.text: What percentage of victims lose their job due to bullying (WBI)?
questions.explanation: WBI studies show that a majority (67-77%) of victims lose their job, either quitting or being fired.

questions.text: What is the 'Bystander Effect'?

options.label: People intervene more when others are present
People don't intervene, expecting others to do so

questions.explanation: Responsibility 'diffuses' when multiple people are present, making intervention less likely.

questions.text: Which bystander role relates to best work engagement?
questions.explanation: Active defending predicts best work engagement for the bystander themselves.

questions.text: What proportion of witnesses do not report what they saw?
questions.explanation: About 55% of witnesses do not report, which is alarmingly high.

questions.text: What is the most common reason for not reporting?
questions.explanation: Cynicism and belief that the organization won't do anything is the top reason (55%).

questions.text: How does the number of passive bystanders affect the victim?
questions.explanation: More passive bystanders amplify the negative effect on the victim.

questions.text: What physical symptoms does long-term bullying cause?
questions.explanation: Bullying triggers severe physiological stress reactions.

questions.text: What is the cardiovascular risk ratio for victims compared to non-victims?
questions.explanation: Risk is 2.3 times higher. Long-term stress is toxic to the body.

questions.text: How does witness well-being compare to victims?
questions.explanation: Witnesses are also traumatized. Watching injustice is psychologically heavy.

questions.text: Where does bullying bank as a stressor?
questions.explanation: It is the 2nd most common stressor after excessive workload.

questions.text: How many victims have told someone?
questions.explanation: Only about half tell anyone. Shame and fear prevent speaking out.

questions.text: Who is responsible for intervening in bullying?
questions.explanation: The employer has a legal duty to intervene immediately when aware.

questions.text: What is the effect of teaching DARVO?
questions.explanation: Knowledge is armor. Recognizing the pattern weakens its effect.

questions.text: Which industry suffers most from bullying?
questions.explanation: Health and social care top the statistics due to hierarchy and pressure.

questions.text: Which gender is more likely to be a victim?
questions.explanation: Women are more often victims (57%), while men are overrepresented as bullies.

questions.text: How many female bullies choose a female victim?
questions.explanation: Female bullies target other women 71% of the time.

questions.text: What is the strongest protective factor?
questions.explanation: Culture eats strategy for breakfast. If management doesn't support zero tolerance, policies are useless.

questions.text: Which is an ineffective prevention method?
questions.explanation: Declarations are not enough if structures don't support them.

questions.text: What does 'culture of silence' mean?
questions.explanation: It allows abuse to continue because no one dares to speak.

questions.text: What is 'institutional betrayal'?
questions.explanation: When the organization that should protect you turns its back, it causes deep trauma.

questions.text: How many UK healthcare workers experienced bullying?
questions.explanation: Public sector pressures are a global challenge.
